A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same InterDyn study. Their main text, equations, figures, five result tables and supplied appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial relocation of material.

before.justification: v2 reports original SSV2 evaluations, generated CLEVRER interaction examples and DexYCB ablation results, including Table 1, Figure 4 and Table 2.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results, including the SSV2 comparisons, CLEVRER examples and DexYCB ablations now in Table S1.

M1.justification: The frozen SVD backbone, trainable ControlNet-style branch, control encoding and inference procedure remain unchanged. The redrawn Figure 3 and corrected input tensor notation describe the existing method.

E1.justification: Both versions use CLEVRER, Something-Something-v2 and DexYCB for the same tasks. The pretending-class evaluation and qualitative interaction scenarios are retained; moving DexYCB to the appendix does not remove coverage.

E2.justification: The main and pretending-class comparisons retain Seer, DynamiCrafter, CosHand-Independent and CosHand-Autoregressive. The second-frame comparison retains the same static baselines, including the separately evaluated CosHand row on the authors' validation set.

E3.justification: The matched experiments retain their splits, sample counts, resolutions, preprocessing, metrics and settings, including 14-frame generation, 7 FPS and 50 denoising steps. The revised DexYCB contour description does not establish a different experimental protocol.

E4.justification: The control-type and occlusion ablations move from Section 4.5 to Appendix A with the same evidence. Counterfactual examples, noisy-mask robustness, failure cases, per-class motion fidelity and pretending-class analyses are also retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. The metric estimators and per-class averaging practices remain unchanged.

E6.justification: All five matched tables retain identical numerical entries: Table 1, v2 Table 2/v3 Table S1, v2 Table S1/v3 Table S2, v2 Table S2/v3 Table S4, and Table S3. The qualitative examples and reported outcomes are also retained.

T1.justification: The motion-fidelity equations and baseline recursions are unchanged. Section 3 adds a singleton image dimension and makes control-channel notation consistent with the existing Control paragraph; this is not a substantive mathematical revision.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about controllable interactive video generation, implicit physical knowledge, generalization to unseen objects and advantages over static state-transition baselines.

C2.justification: v3 Appendix A explicitly acknowledges that hand-mask contours can reveal object trajectory as well as shape; v2 Section 4.5 mentioned shape only. The other mechanism interpretations and failure limitations are retained, with failure discussion consolidated in Appendix C.

D1.justification: The abstract replaces 'Code and trained models will be released' with a generic project-page reference at the same address. This removes an explicit release commitment without establishing any actual availability change. Implementation and preprocessing details otherwise remain available.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning remain unchanged. The bibliography decreases from 107 to 106 entries by merging duplicate ControlNet references; subsequent renumbering and an author-name accent correction are bibliographic cleanup.

P1.justification: Targeted prose tightening accompanies moving the ablation section to Appendix A and combining failure and per-class discussions in Appendix C. Other appendix sections are reordered, and the inline MJB conflict disclosure becomes a link. Most main-text language and narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 3 is completely redesigned with a different pipeline layout and clearer encoding, concatenation and frozen/trainable labels. Visual evidence is substantially reorganized: Figure 8/Table 2 move to the appendix, Figure 7 precedes Table 1, and the limitations figure and class table are regrouped. These changes redisplay existing content.

improvement.justification: The clearer Figure 3, more concise explanations and consolidated limitations evidence make the unchanged study easier to follow. Explicitly acknowledging trajectory leakage also improves qualification of the control signal. These are limited gains: scientific support is unchanged, limitations become less prominent outside the main text, and replacing the release promise and inline conflict disclosure with general or external references reduces self-containment.
